framework: Seven-gate pre-deployment AIA for population-health risk tools

gates.name: Inventory & intended use
gates.question: What decision does the tool inform, for whom, at what capacity, and what exactly does it predict?
gates.evidence: Vendor documentation stating the label, features, training population and intended use; local decision map.
gates.criterion: The label and intended use are written down and match. A mismatch (predicts cost, used for need) is flagged for G1.
gates.hooks: 45 CFR 92.210(b); EU AI Act Arts 13, 26; Bias Playbook step 1

retro.note: The vendor's label (cost) was known, but the mismatch with the programme's purpose (need) was never flagged.

gates.name: Label validity
gates.question: Does the training target measure the construct of interest equally well across groups?
gates.evidence: Mean need (active chronic conditions, biomarkers) by score percentile and group; within-percentile gap with 95% CI, especially in the threshold band.
gates.criterion: Upper 95% bound of the need gap in the selection band below 0.25 conditions, or relative gap under 5%.
gates.hooks: EU AI Act Art 10(2)(f)–(g); ICMR principle of validity; NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.11

retro.note: Selection band: Black patients carry about 1.4 more conditions (+27%). Within-percentile gap 0.61 (CI 0.56–0.67).

gates.name: Disparity testing
gates.question: At the operating threshold, who is selected compared with who is truly high-need, by race, sex, age, insurance and language?
gates.evidence: Representation ratio, recall and precision against a capacity-matched need group; sensitivity to the definition of need.
gates.criterion: Representation ratio of at least 0.9 for every group, and no group held to a visibly higher bar (precision gap under 10 points).
gates.hooks: 45 CFR 92.210(c); EU AI Act Art 4a (bias data); DPDP Act s.8(3)

retro.note: Our test gives a representation ratio of 0.80 at the 97th percentile. Selected Black patients are high-need 47% of the time, against 33% for White patients.

gates.name: Rights & stakeholder review
gates.question: Who could be harmed, how badly, and can it be reversed? What do affected patients and clinicians say?
gates.evidence: Fundamental-rights / data-protection impact assessment; patient and community panel; impact level I–IV.
gates.criterion: Panel held, impact level assigned, and its requirements adopted (Level III–IV for this tool).
gates.hooks: EU AI Act Art 27 (FRIA); GDPR Art 35 (DPIA); DPDP Rules r.13

retro.note: No record of patient engagement or a rights assessment before deployment.

gates.name: Mitigation & oversight design
gates.question: What changes reduce the harm, and does human review actually correct the tool?
gates.evidence: Label blend evaluated on the fairness–cost frontier; override protocol; audit of clinician decisions by group; automation-bias training.
gates.criterion: G1 and G2 pass after mitigation; enrolled patients equally sick across groups.
gates.hooks: EU AI Act Arts 14, 26(2); Colorado SB 26-189 human review

retro.note: Clinician review existed but did not correct the bias: enrolled Black patients had 1.24 more conditions.

gates.name: Go / no-go & publication
gates.question: Who signs off, on what evidence, and what is made public?
gates.evidence: Signed decision by an accountable executive; public summary of the AIA; entry in an algorithm register.
gates.criterion: Named accountable owner; summary published before launch.
gates.hooks: Canada DADM publication duty; EU AI Act Art 49 registration

retro.note: No public assessment or named accountable owner.

gates.name: Monitoring & re-assessment
gates.question: How will drift, complaints and new evidence trigger a re-run of G1–G2?
gates.evidence: Quarterly calibration-by-group dashboard; incident log; re-assessment triggers (new population, new threshold, new vendor version).
gates.criterion: G1–G2 re-run at least annually and on every trigger; results reported to the governance committee.
gates.hooks: 45 CFR 92.210 (ongoing); EU AI Act Art 26(5), Art 72

retro.note: Bias found by external researchers in 2019, not by internal monitoring.

impact_levels.label: Moderate impact
impact_levels.requires: Notice, peer review or expert consultation, explanation on request

impact_levels.label: High impact
impact_levels.requires: Peer review, published AIA, human makes the final decision, ongoing monitoring

impact_levels.label: Very high impact
impact_levels.requires: All of Level III plus two independent reviews and executive sign-off
